propertyFacts.label: coproduct evolution
propertyFacts.value: Initial O,O-diphenyl carbonate and oleic anhydride formation is reported for 1e, followed by conversion into other products; the source does not identify the later 1e products in this main-text comparison.
propertyFacts.scope: Main p2 explicitly includes 1c and 1e in the initial carbonate/anhydride observation. The named p-tolyl oleate/p-cresol evolution and Scheme 3 are the separate 1c context; no final-product identity or kinetic trajectory is transferred to 1e.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
